# Isaiah Chapter 9 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folio 145v | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/ISA_009_page_001.jpg

---

**9:2** The-people [ha-am] who-walk [ha-holkhim] in-the-darkness [ba-choshekh] have-seen [ra'u] a-great [gadol] light [or]; those-who-dwell [yoshevei] in-the-land of-the-shadow-of-death [tsalmavvet] — light [or] has-shone [nagah] upon-them [alehem].

**9:6** For a-child [yeled] is-born [yullad] to-us, a-son [ben] is-given [nittan] to-us, and-the-government [ha-misrah] will-be upon his-shoulder [shikhmo]; and-his-name [shemo] will-be-called [vayyiqra] Wonderful [pele] Counselor [yo'ets], Mighty [gibbor] God [El], Everlasting [ad] Father [avi], Prince [sar] of-Peace [shalom].

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.6 — The throne names:** Four throne names in two pairs: *Pele-Yo'ets* (Wonderful Counselor), *El-Gibbor* (Mighty God), *Avi-Ad* (Everlasting Father), *Sar-Shalom* (Prince of Peace). These are royal throne names given at coronation — not necessarily claims of divinity but of divine empowerment. Whether this refers to Hezekiah, a future Davidic king, or a messianic figure is the central debate.

*— EMET*
